```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2"],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the browser game request, its boundaries, and discovery defaults.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: Deliver a small browser-playable Battleship game for one human against a computer opponent; the browser is the player’s entry point. Assumption: The game uses a conventional Battleship ruleset, with exact board, fleet, placement, and win rules recorded during discovery; this rules out treating any particular variant as requested. Assumption: One browser session represents one anonymous player, with no accounts, multiplayer, cross-device sharing, or persistence; discovery must establish what the runtime already provides before confirming session identification and state handling. Assumption: Game state lasts for the active session until a new game, reset, or session end; discovery must establish the available runtime lifecycle before finalizing those transitions. Assumption: Each side’s unhit ship positions remain hidden from the opponent, while the player can see their own board and shot results; discovery must establish the chosen rules and state boundary before finalizing information visibility. Open question: Discovery determines the browser interaction flow, computer turn behavior, and accessible controls from the request and available evidence; these block interaction design. Open question: Discovery identifies the intended usable target and any delivery or release mechanism from workspace and team evidence; this blocks target-specific delivery, and a target named by the request would itself grant delivery authority. Source hints, not verified facts: the team or workspace, relevant channels, internal sites and documents, private repositories, owners, and the ambiguous term ‘small’; discovery should resolve these from evidence rather than a questionnaire. Sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. S2 — Fact: Use Node.js for the server and include tests; discovery determines the existing runtime, dependencies, test conventions, and testable game behaviors before selecting the implementation and validation approach. Boundary: The repository is empty, this unattended run performs intake only, and no implementation is authorized in this stage. Visibility: Work in an isolated run becomes visible in its source checkout at final return; a deployed outcome becomes usable in its target only after release. No prior run is identified."
}
```
